question: What is the concept of stare decisis?
options: The principle that a court should follow the decisions of higher courts and previous decisions of the same court, so as to maintain consistency and predictability in the application of the law.
The principle that a court should follow the decisions of its peers
The principle that a court should follow the decisions of foreign courts
The principle that a court should not follow the decisions of previous courts

question: Which of the following is a characteristic of a limited liability company?
options: A company that has unlimited personal liability for its shareholders
A company that has limited personal liability for its shareholders
A company that has limited personal liability for its employees
A company that has unlimited personal liability for its employees

question: What is the principle of res ipsa loquitur in tort law?
options: The principle that where an injury is so ordinary and foreseeable that it could have occurred in the absence of negligence, the court may infer negligence on the part of the defendant
The principle that where an injury is so ordinary and foreseeable that it could have occurred in the absence of negligence, the court may not infer negligence on the part of the defendant
The principle that where an injury is so extraordinary and unforeseeable that it could not have occurred in the absence of negligence, the court may infer negligence on the part of the defendant.
The principle that where an injury is so extraordinary and unforeseeable that it could not have occurred in the absence of negligence, the court may not infer negligence on the part of the defendant

question: What is the principle of proportionality in human rights law?
options: The principle that a restriction on a fundamental right must not be proportionate to the aim being pursued
The principle that a restriction on a fundamental right must be proportionate to the interest of the individual
The principle that a restriction on a fundamental right must be proportionate to the aim being pursued
The principle that a restriction on a fundamental right must not be proportionate to the interest of the individual

question: Which of the following is a characteristic of a sole trader?
options: One person carrying on a business in their own name with unlimited personal liability
One person carrying on a business in a partnership with unlimited personal liability
One person carrying on a business in a partnership with limited personal liability
Two or more people carrying on a business in a partnership with unlimited personal liability

question: What is the doctrine of estoppel in contract law?
options: The doctrine that a party will not be prevented from denying a fact if it has acted in a way that is inconsistent with that fact unless they have been negligent
The doctrine that a party will be prevented from denying a fact if it has acted in a way that is inconsistent with that fact
The doctrine that a party will not be prevented from denying a fact if it has acted in a way that is consistent with that fact
The doctrine that a party will be prevented from denying a fact if it has not acted in a way that is inconsistent with that fact

question: What is the doctrine of caveat emptor in contract law?
options: The doctrine that a buyer can only sue the seller for defects or flaws in a property or commodity that are not obvious or apparent
The doctrine that a seller must disclose all defects or flaws in a property or a commodity to the buyer
The doctrine that a buyer must take a property or a commodity in its existing state and cannot sue the seller for any defects or flaws
The doctrine that a buyer can sue the seller for any defects or flaws in a property or a commodity

One or more persons carrying on a business in common with a view to profit
One or more persons carrying on a business in common with a view to a non-profit motive

A company where two or more people are jointly and severally liable for the company's debts and obligations
A company where one person is solely liable for the company's debts and obligations

question: What is the doctrine of privity of contract in contract law?

The doctrine that a person who is not a party to a contract can only sue or be sued on the contract if they have a legitimate interest in doing so

The doctrine that a person may be prevented from enforcing a contract if they have been influenced or coerced by another person into not entering into the contract
The doctrine that a person may be prevented from enforcing a contract if they have been influenced or coerced by another person into entering into the contract
